title: Black Obelisk
summary: A Neo-Assyrian monument showing tribute scenes, including a figure often identified as Jehu.
historical_context: One of the most famous visual sources for biblical-era Near Eastern diplomacy.
ancient_near_east_context: The item belongs to the broader imperial, cultic, and urban world of the ancient Near East and the biblical periods reflected in the dataset.
literary_context: Frequently linked to the political world of Jehu and the Omride dynasty.
covenantal_significance: Black Obelisk helps anchor biblical claims in historical reality while reminding readers that archaeology supports rather than replaces interpretation.
interpretive_notes: The Jehu identification is widely accepted, but the monument still functions as royal ideology, not neutral reportage.
Use the item as context for the biblical text, not as a shortcut around it.
